_comment: Dashboard telltale catalogue used by services/warning_lights.py to identify
an uploaded warning-light image without needing a vision model.
Each entry carries the geometric signature of the ISO/ECE symbol as it is
normally drawn: colour, the bounding-box aspect ratio of the glyph, how much
of that box the ink fills, how many enclosed holes the symbol has, and
whether it is left-right symmetric. Ranges are deliberately wide — the goal
is to rank candidates, not to claim a single answer from geometry alone.
kb_id links to data/repair_knowledge.json so an identified light inherits
real causes and Indian repair costs instead of the model inventing them.

lights.name: Battery / charging system
lights.meaning: The battery is not being charged. Usually the alternator, its belt, or the battery itself.
lights.urgency: The car is running on battery alone and will stop when it is flat. Drive straight to a garage or call for help.

lights.name: Engine oil pressure
lights.meaning: Engine oil pressure has dropped below the safe threshold.
lights.urgency: Stop the engine immediately. Driving on low oil pressure destroys the engine within minutes.

lights.name: Coolant temperature
lights.urgency: Pull over and let the engine cool. Do not open the radiator cap while hot.

lights.name: Check engine (MIL)
lights.meaning: The engine management system has logged a fault. Needs an OBD scan to read the code.
lights.urgency: Safe to drive gently if the car feels normal. Get the fault code read soon. If it is flashing, stop — that means a misfire that can destroy the catalytic converter.

lights.name: Brake system
lights.meaning: Parking brake engaged, low brake fluid, or a brake system fault.
lights.urgency: Check the handbrake is fully released. If it stays lit, treat the brakes as unreliable and stop.

lights.name: ABS
lights.meaning: The anti-lock braking system has faulted. Normal braking still works; ABS assistance does not.
lights.urgency: Drive gently and leave extra stopping distance, especially in the wet. Get it checked.

lights.name: Airbag / SRS
lights.meaning: A fault in the airbag system. The airbags may not deploy in a crash.
lights.urgency: The car drives normally but its crash protection is compromised. Get it repaired promptly.

lights.name: TPMS (tyre pressure)
lights.meaning: One or more tyres is significantly under-inflated, or a TPMS sensor has faulted.
lights.urgency: Check and inflate all four tyres. A slow puncture is the usual cause.

lights.name: Power steering (EPS)
lights.meaning: Electric power steering assistance has faulted.
lights.urgency: The steering may become very heavy, especially at low speed. Drive slowly to a garage.

lights.name: DPF (diesel particulate filter)
lights.meaning: The diesel particulate filter is clogged and needs regeneration.
lights.urgency: Drive at steady highway speed for 20 minutes to let it regenerate. If it stays lit, get it serviced.

lights.name: Glow plug (diesel preheat)
lights.meaning: Normal during cold start. If it stays lit or flashes, a glow plug or its relay has failed.
lights.urgency: Hard starting in cold weather is the usual symptom. Book a service.
